brief.scope: Independently assess the boundary required by scope-conductor-start.txt: an interactive codex/claude/grok conductor with forwarded CLI args and no manual approval interruptions. No implementation exists. Measure the installed CLI and OS capabilities; recommend the smallest usable protections against destructive host/repository/remote actions. Distinguish actual enforcement from hooks or prompt policy. Consider writable git common directories, isolated workspaces/state, credentials, network and host sockets, child workers, symlink paths, and parameter overrides. Preserve normal conductor dispatch, git/PR work and context access. Do not change settings, rulesets, source, or tests. Return a concise feasibility ruling with concrete expected/found/needed evidence and limits; do not require arbitrary owner approvals already superseded by this work order. Review/design evidence only, not an implementation review. Avoid broad repository onboarding and unrelated findings.

artifacts.ruling: Feasible as a contract-first change, but no protection exists yet. The smallest usable boundary is an external bubblewrap sandbox around a private clone and isolated session state, with narrow dispatch and forge brokers. Approval-bypass flags operate only inside that boundary.
artifacts.change_evidence: Expected: scope only, without implementation. Found: the base is an ancestor; the diff adds only .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-conductor-start.txt and passes git diff --check. Needed: the planned contract, independent acceptance tests, then implementation.
artifacts.cli_evidence: Expected: codex, claude and grok support interactive operation without approval pauses. Found: codex-cli 0.153.4 has approval/sandbox overrides and multi_agent=true; Claude Code 2.1.260 has bypassPermissions, add-dir, settings, plugins and agents; grok 1.0.13 has --always-approve, --sandbox, --no-subagents, plugins and leader sockets. Needed: fixed no-prompt flags inside external confinement and a versioned allowlist that refuses safety-affecting forwarded flags.
artifacts.os_evidence: Expected: vendor-neutral enforcement. Found: Ubuntu 24.04.4 on WSL2; bubblewrap 0.9.0 and user namespaces work; basic and shared-network bwrap probes exited 0. AppArmor is disabled, nft/iptables/slirp are absent, and bwrap network isolation failed under the current seccomp filter. Needed: fail-closed mount, user and PID isolation; network isolation requires an added egress mechanism or must remain an explicit limit.
artifacts.filesystem_boundary: Use a private non-shared clone so the main checkout and writable git common directory are absent. Mount only required system files read-only, the private clone and new session state writable, and named context inputs read-only. Do not ro-bind the host root: read-only mounts still expose credentials and sockets. Open mount roots without following symlinks and bind by file descriptor; refuse symlinked roots or ancestors before side effects.
artifacts.credentials_and_remote: Found: model credential files and gh hosts.yml exist mode 0600; gh authentication is currently invalid and the snapshot has no remote, so PR behavior was not testable. Docker access was denied, but /run/user/1006/bus and the WSL interop socket are exposed. Needed: mask all host sockets and homes, sanitize remotes and Git credential helpers, withhold forge/SSH credentials, and expose only a broker permitting fast-forward pushes to the session branch and non-destructive draft-PR operations. Refuse force/delete, protected-branch updates, merge/close, rulesets and repository administration.
artifacts.dispatch_and_children: Hide direct worker-launch surfaces; expose a narrow broker that validates structured requests and invokes ops/bin/dispatch.sh externally. Disable Codex multi_agent, pass Grok --no-subagents, and remove Claude Agent/Task/Workflow tools. These CLI controls and the existing Claude hook enforce tool availability only when their configuration cannot be overridden; hooks and prompts are not host protection.
artifacts.argument_contract: Parse the conductor selector separately and forward permitted argument tokens byte-for-byte without eval. Reserve and refuse cwd/add-dir/worktree, sandbox/permission, config/profile/settings, plugin/MCP, remote/socket, credential, system-prompt/rules, agent/subagent and feature-toggle options, including aliases and key=value forms. Unknown options on a changed CLI version must refuse with expected-found-needed evidence.
artifacts.acceptance: Independent cases should prove: each harness launches through a PTY without approval; safe arguments retain exact token boundaries; conflicting or unknown safety arguments refuse before writes; normal commit, dispatch and draft-PR work succeeds; main checkout/common-dir/config/session hashes remain unchanged; protected refs and destructive forge calls fail; host sockets and credentials are absent; symlink escapes fail; direct child workers fail while brokered dispatch succeeds.
artifacts.limits: Shared networking permits access to localhost and arbitrary endpoints; readable model credentials can still be stolen or abused by a compromised harness; vendor services receive readable context by design; brokers and CLI behavior remain new trusted components. These risks cannot be claimed prevented until egress and credential mediation are independently demonstrated.
artifacts.proposed_files: Contract/profile under ops/conductor/contracts/; launcher shim under ops/bin/; implementation and narrow brokers under ops/conductor/tools/; independently authored contract, symlink, socket, argument, Git and remote acceptance tests under ops/conductor/tests/.

envelope.note: Approval covers the work-order scope and feasibility only; it does not attest that an enforcement boundary is presently implemented.
